# Set Up

```{r}
#| label: set-up
# Import Libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(mgcv)
library(kableExtra)
library(ComplexUpset)
library(broom)
library(psych)
library(ggseg)
library(BifactorIndicesCalculator)
library(effectsize)
library(scales)

# Source
source("R/mapping.R")
source("R/plotting.R")
source("R/reporting.R")

# Define Paths
dir_dataset <- file.path(
  "/", "data", "secure", "bit_repo", "projects_repo", "ExtraLong", "data",
  "dataset_pnc_cross"
)

dir_evolpsy <- file.path(
  "/", "data", "secure", "bit_repo", "pi_repo", "raquel_gur", "evolpsy", "data"
)

dir_cnb <- file.path(
  "/", "data", "secure", "bit_repo", "projects_repo", "ExtraLong", "data",
  "long_cnb"
)

path_imaging <- file.path(dir_dataset, "imaging_data.csv")
path_sub_ses <- file.path(dir_dataset, "subjects_sessions.csv")

path_merge <- file.path(
  dir_evolpsy, "go1_files", "pncgo1_data_merge_mar2025.csv"
)

path_env_ses <- file.path(dir_evolpsy, "zac_data", "env_scores.csv")
path_env_trauma <- file.path(dir_evolpsy, "zac_data", "env_for_zac.csv")

path_goassess <- file.path(
  "/", "data", "secure", "bit_repo", "projects_repo", "goassess_scoring",
  "tests", "data", "n9498_goassess_psych_summary_vars_20131014.csv"
)

path_imglook <-
  file.path("/", "data", "secure", "bit_dwh", "oracle", "imglook.csv")

path_new_cnb <-
  file.path(
    "/", "data", "secure", "bit_repo", "projects_repo", "ExtraLong", "data",
    "cnb_accuracy_speed_commonsmryscores_allbbl_longform.csv"
  )

path_cnb_accuracy <- file.path(dir_cnb, "BIG_CNB_Accuracy_Longitudinal_Factor_Scores_FullBattery.csv")
path_cnb_efficiency <- file.path(dir_cnb, "BIG_CNB_Efficiency_Longitudinal_Factor_Scores_FullBattery.csv")
path_cnb_speed <- file.path(dir_cnb, "BIG_CNB_Speed_Longitudinal_Factor_Scores_FullBattery.csv")

# Read Data
raw_imaging <- read_csv(path_imaging)
raw_sub_ses <- read_csv(path_sub_ses)

raw_merge <- read_csv(path_merge)

raw_env_ses <- read_csv(path_env_ses)
raw_env_trauma <- read_csv(path_env_trauma)

raw_goassess <- read_csv(path_goassess)

raw_cnb_accuracy <- read_csv(path_cnb_accuracy)
raw_cnb_efficiency <- read_csv(path_cnb_efficiency)
raw_cnb_speed <- read_csv(path_cnb_speed)
```

# Clean Data

```{r}
#| label: clean-data
# Demographics
demo <-
  left_join(
    raw_sub_ses |>
      select(bblid, scanid, age),
    raw_merge |>
      rename(dx = clinical_goassessDxpmr7) |>
      select(bblid, sex, race, dx),
    by = join_by(bblid),
    relationship = "one-to-one"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    age = age / 12,
    dx = factor(dx, levels = c("TD", "PS", "OP")),
    race = factor(
      race,
      levels = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 9),
      labels = c(
        "White",
        "Black",
        "Native American",
        "Asian",
        "Biracial",
        "Hawaiian/Pacific Islander",
        "Unknown"
      )
    ),
    sex = factor(sex, levels = c(1, 2), labels = c("Male", "Female"))
  ) |>
  arrange(bblid, scanid)

# Environment
env <- full_join(raw_env_ses, raw_env_trauma, by = join_by(bblid), relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  clean_names() |>
  rename(trauma = trauma_exposure, ses = env_ses) |>
  select(bblid, trauma, ses)

# Imaging
imaging_qc <- raw_sub_ses |>
  mutate(qc = cume_dist(euler)) |>
  filter(qc > 0.01) |>
  select(bblid, scanid)

imaging <- raw_imaging |>
  filter(atlas == "desikan_killiany", !is.na(lobe)) |>
  semi_join(imaging_qc, by = join_by(bblid, scanid)) |>
  pivot_wider(values_from = value, names_from = metric) |>
  select(bblid, scanid, lobe, laterality, region, lgi, area) |>
  drop_na()

global_lgi <- imaging |>
  summarize(lgi = weighted.mean(lgi, area), .by = c(bblid, scanid))

lgi_lobe <- imaging |>
  summarize(lgi = weighted.mean(lgi, area), .by = c(bblid, scanid, lobe)) |>
  mutate(lobe = factor(
    str_to_title(lobe),
    levels = c("Frontal", "Parietal", "Occipital", "Temporal", "Cingulate")
  ))

global_volume <- raw_imaging |>
  filter(region == "BrainSegVolNotVent") |>
  semi_join(imaging_qc, by = join_by(bblid, scanid)) |>
  rename(volume = value) |>
  select(bblid, scanid, volume) |>
  drop_na()

# Clinical
clinical <- raw_merge |>
  semi_join(demo, by = join_by(bblid)) |>
  select(
    bblid,
    starts_with("clinical_longfactor") &
      (contains("bifactor") | contains("corrTraits"))
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = -bblid, names_to = "name", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(
    type = name |> str_split("_") |> map_chr(3) |> str_to_snake(),
    factor = factor(
      name |>
        str_replace("General_p", "GeneralP") |>
        str_split("_") |>
        map_chr(4) |>
        str_to_snake() |>
        str_replace_all("_", " ") |>
        str_to_title() |>
        str_replace_all("Adhd", "ADHD"),
      levels = c(
        "General P",
        "ADHD",
        "Depression",
        "Mania",
        "Psychosis Negative",
        "Psychosis Positive"
      )
    )
      
  ) |>
  select(bblid, type, factor, value)

# Cognitive
bblid_doscan <-
  read_csv(path_imglook) |>
  clean_names() |>
  semi_join(demo, by = join_by(bblid, scanid)) |>
  select(bblid, scanid, doscan) |>
  mutate(doscan = lubridate::mdy(doscan))

cnb_dump <-
  read_csv(
    path_new_cnb,
    col_select = c(
      test_sessions.datasetid,
      test_sessions.bblid,
      test_sessions_v.dotest
    )
  ) |>
  rename_with(\(x) {map_chr(str_split(x, "\\."), 2)})

datasetid_mapping <-
  inner_join(bblid_doscan, cnb_dump, by = join_by(bblid), relationship = "one-to-many") |>
  mutate(time_difference = abs(as.numeric(difftime(doscan, dotest, units = "days")))) |>
  slice_min(order_by = time_difference, n = 1, by = c(bblid, scanid), with_ties = TRUE) |>
  filter(time_difference < 30.5 * 6) |>
  select(bblid, scanid, datasetid)

cnb <-
  full_join(
    raw_cnb_accuracy |>
      select(datasetid, ends_with("Accuracy_AgeReg")),
    raw_cnb_efficiency |>
      select(datasetid, ends_with("Efficiency_AgeReg")),
    by = join_by(datasetid),
    relationship = "one-to-one"
  ) |>
  full_join(
    raw_cnb_speed |>
      select(datasetid, ends_with("Speed_AgeReg")),
    by = join_by(datasetid),
    relationship = "one-to-one"
  ) |>
  inner_join(
    datasetid_mapping,
    by = join_by(datasetid),
    relationship = "one-to-one"
  ) |>
  select(-datasetid) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(bblid, scanid),
    names_to = "name",
    values_to = "value"
  ) |>
  separate_wider_delim(
    name,
    delim = "_",
    names = c("domain", "measure", NA)
  ) |>
  filter(domain != "Discounting") |>
  mutate(
    domain = factor(
      str_replace(domain, "SocialCog", "Social"),
      levels = c("Overall", "Executive", "Memory", "Complex", "Social", "Motor")
    ),
    measure = factor(
      replace_when(measure, domain == "Motor" & measure == "Efficiency" ~ "Speed"),
      levels = c("Accuracy", "Efficiency", "Speed")
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(bblid, scanid, measure, domain) |>
  drop_na()

# GOASSESS
psy_symptoms <- c(
  "smry_del", "smry_hal_av", "smry_hal_as", "smry_hal_vh", "smry_hal_oh",
  "smry_hal_th", "smry_hal"
)

goassess_disorder <-
  raw_goassess |>
  semi_join(demo, by = join_by(bblid)) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = -bblid, names_to = "disorder", values_to = "score") |>
  filter(!str_ends(disorder, "_cat")) |>
  mutate(
    category = case_when(
      disorder %in% c(
        "smry_agr", "smry_gad", "smry_ocd", "smry_pan", "smry_phb", "smry_ptd",
        "smry_sep", "smry_soc"
      ) ~ "anx",
      disorder %in% c("smry_add", "smry_odd", "smry_con") ~ "beh",
      disorder %in% c("smry_ano", "smry_bul") ~ "eat",
      disorder %in% c("smry_dep", "smry_man") ~ "mood",
      disorder %in% c(
        "smry_del", "smry_hal_av", "smry_hal_as", "smry_hal_vh", "smry_hal_oh",
        "smry_hal_th", "smry_hal"
      ) ~ "psy"
    ),
    disorder = goassess_mapping[disorder],
    status = case_when(
      score == 4 & category != "psy" ~ TRUE,
      score == 3 & category == "psy" ~ TRUE,
      score %in% 0:3 & category != "psy" ~ FALSE,
      score %in% 0:2 & category == "psy" ~ FALSE,
    )
  )

goassess_category <-
  raw_goassess |>
  semi_join(demo, by = join_by(bblid)) |>
  select(bblid, ends_with("_cat")) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = -bblid, names_to = "category", values_to = "score") |>
  mutate(
    category = goassess_category_mapping[category],
    status = case_when(
      score == 4 ~ TRUE,
      score %in% 0:3 ~ FALSE,
    )
  )
```

# Sample Description

The following analyses use the GO1 imaging sample.

## Subsample

The "Clean Subsample" consists of people where LGI data is available, who did not endorse any trauma exposures, who reported their race as "White", who are Typically Developing according to `Dxpmrv7`. Within each sex, the 25 eligible individuals with brain parenchymal volume, `BrainSegVolNotVent`, closest to the sex-specific median volume of the full sample were selected.

```{r}
#| label: subsample
clean_subsample <-
  inner_join(demo, global_volume, by = join_by(bblid), relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  mutate(volume_median = median(volume), .by = sex) |>
  semi_join(drop_na(global_lgi), by = join_by(bblid)) |>
  semi_join(filter(env, trauma == 0), by = join_by(bblid)) |>
  filter(race == "White", dx == "TD") |>
  slice_min(abs(volume - volume_median), n = 25, with_ties = FALSE, by = sex) |>
  select(bblid) |>
  arrange(bblid)
```

::: {.content-visible when-profile="scratch"}

```{r}
#| label: demos-table
demo_table <-

row_hierarchy <- demo_table |>

    Category = c("n", "age", "sex", "sex", "dx", "dx", "dx", "env", "env"),
```

## LGI-Volume Tertile Groups

```{r}
#| label: tertile-groups
#| control: {method: residual, variables: [age, sex]}
#| scale: global
data_lgi_vol_tertile <-
  inner_join(global_lgi, global_volume, by = join_by(bblid, scanid), relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  inner_join(demo, by = join_by(bblid), relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  select(bblid, lgi, volume, age, sex) |>
  mutate(
    across(
      c(lgi, volume),
      \(x) residuals(gam(x ~ s(age) + sex))
    ),
    group = str_c("g", ntile(lgi, 3), "v", ntile(volume, 3))
  ) |>
  select(bblid, group, lgi, volume)

lgi_vol_tertile_groups <- data_lgi_vol_tertile |> select(bblid, group)

plot_lgi_vol_tertile <-
  ggplot(
    data = data_lgi_vol_tertile,
    mapping = aes(x = lgi, y = volume, color = group)
  ) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.75, size = 1) +
  color_scale_group +
  labs(
    x = "Global LGI",
    y = "Brain Parenchymal Volume"
  ) +
  theme_linedraw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

plot_lgi_vol_tertile
```

# Local Gyrification Index

Local Gyrification Index (LGI) is a measure of cortical gyrification. Prior to calculating LGI, the FreeSurfer pipeline has already reconstructed the pial surface. To calculate LGI FreeSurfer performs morphological closing, which is analogous to wrapping the cortical surface tightly in cellophane. LGI is then the ratio between the surface area of the pial surface and this abstract outer surface, calculated locally at many points across the cortex.

## Relationship Between LGI and Volume

### Global LGI vs Brain Parenchymal Volume

There is a significant positive correlation between Global LGI and Brain Parenchymal Volume $r = 0.438, 95\% CI [0.397, 0.478], p < .001$.

```{r}
#| label: lgi-volume-global
#| test: {method: correlation, variables: [lgi, volume]}
#| control: {method: residual, variables: [age, sex]}
#| scale: global
data_lgi_volume_global <-
  inner_join(global_lgi, global_volume, by = join_by(bblid, scanid), relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  inner_join(demo, by = join_by(bblid, scanid), relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  drop_na(bblid, scanid, lgi, volume, age, sex) |>
  mutate(
    lgi = residuals(gam(lgi ~ s(age) + sex)),
    volume = residuals(gam(volume ~ s(age) + sex))
  ) |>
  select(bblid, scanid, lgi, volume)

test_lgi_volume_global <- cor.test(data_lgi_volume_global$lgi, data_lgi_volume_global$volume)

test_lgi_volume_global

plot_lgi_volume_global <-
  ggplot(data = data_lgi_volume_global, mapping = aes(x = volume, y = lgi)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.25, size = 1) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm",
    formula = y ~ x,
    se = TRUE,
    color = "black",
    fill = "black",
    linewidth = 0.75,
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Correlation of Global LGI and Brain Parenchymal Volume",
    subtitle = report_correlation(test_lgi_volume_global),
    x = "Brain Parenchymal Volume",
    y = "Global LGI"
  ) +
  theme_linedraw()

plot_lgi_volume_global
```

### Regional LGI vs Volume

LGI was significantly correlated with volume in all cortical brain regions except the left temporal pole. The strength of the correlation varied widely, from very weak ($r = 0.0832$) in the right temporal pole to very strong ($r = 0.667$) in the right rostral middle frontal area.

::: {.collapsible-table data-rows="5"}

```{r}
#| label: lgi-volume-regional
#| test: {method: correlation, variables: [lgi, volume]}
#| control: {method: residual, variables: [age, sex]}
#| scale: region
data_lgi_volume <-
  raw_imaging |>
  filter(metric %in% c("lgi", "volume"), atlas == "desikan_killiany") |>
  pivot_wider(values_from = value, names_from = metric) |>
  inner_join(demo, by = join_by(bblid, scanid), relationship = "many-to-one") |>
  drop_na(bblid, scanid, laterality, region, lgi, volume, age, sex) |>
  mutate(region = str_c(laterality, region, sep = "_")) |>
  mutate(
    lgi = residuals(gam(lgi ~ s(age) + sex)),
    volume = residuals(gam(volume ~ s(age) + sex)),
    .by = region
  ) |>
  select(bblid, scanid, region, lgi, volume)

test_lgi_volume <- data_lgi_volume |>
  summarize(
    cor.test(lgi, volume) |>
      tidy() |>
      clean_names(),
    .by = region
  ) |>
  separate(region, into = c("laterality", "region"), sep = "_") |>
  rename(
    r = estimate,
    p = p_value
  ) |>
  mutate(
    region = roi_mapping[region],
    laterality = str_to_title(laterality),
    ci = sprintf("[%.3f, %.3f]", conf_low, conf_high),
    p_fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "fdr"),
    significance = case_when(
      p_fdr < 0.001 ~ "***",
      p_fdr < 0.01 ~ "**",
      p_fdr < 0.05 ~ "*",
      TRUE ~ ""
    )
  )

test_lgi_volume |>
  select(region, laterality, r, ci, p, p_fdr, significance) |>
  arrange(region, laterality) |>
  kbl(
    col.names = c("Region", "Laterality", "r", "95% CI", "p", "pFDR", ""),
    align = "llrrrrl",
    digits = c(NA, NA, 3, NA, 5, 5, NA)
  )

plot_lgi_volume <-
  ggplot() +
  geom_brain(
    atlas = dk(),
    data = test_lgi_volume |>
      mutate(
        region = str_replace_all(
          setNames(names(roi_mapping), roi_mapping)[region],
          ggseg_mapping
        ),
        hemi = str_to_lower(laterality),
        r = replace_when(r, p_fdr >= 0.05 ~ NA)
      ),
    mapping = aes(fill = r),
    position = position_brain(view ~ hemi)
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() +
  labs(
    title = "Regional Correlations Between LGI and Volume",
    caption = "Only correlations with pFDR < 0.05 are shown.",
    fill = "Pearson's r"
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0))

plot_lgi_volume
```

:::

## Regionality of Relationship Between LGI and Psychosis

### Regional LGI vs Psychosis Factor

At the region level in the full sample, after regressing `s(age) + sex` out of regional LGI and psychosis factors, no regions were found where LGI was significantly associated with psychosis.

::: {.collapsible-table data-rows="5"}

```{r}
#| label: lgi-psy-regional-factor
#| test: {method: lm, dv: [psychosis positive, psychosis negative], iv: lgi}
#| control: {method: residual, variables: [age, sex]}
#| scale: region
data_regional_lgi <-
  full_join(
    demo |>
      select(bblid, age, sex),
    imaging |>
      mutate(region = str_c(region, laterality, sep = "_")) |>
      rename(regional_lgi = lgi) |>
      select(bblid, region, regional_lgi),
    by = join_by(bblid),
    relationship = "one-to-many"    
  ) |>
  drop_na() |>
  mutate(
    regional_lgi = residuals(gam(regional_lgi ~ s(age) + sex)),
    .by = region
  ) |>
  select(-age, -sex)

data_regional_psy <-
  full_join(
    demo |>
      select(bblid, age, sex),
    clinical |>
      filter(
        type == "bifactor",
        factor %in% c("Psychosis Positive", "Psychosis Negative")
      ) |>
      rename(psychosis = value) |>
      select(bblid, factor, psychosis),
    by = join_by(bblid),
    relationship = "one-to-many"
  ) |>
  drop_na() |>
  mutate(
    psychosis = residuals(gam(psychosis ~ s(age) + sex)),
    .by = factor
  ) |>
  mutate(factor = str_to_title(str_replace_all(factor, "_", " "))) |>
  select(-age, -sex)

data_lgi_psy_regional <-
  inner_join(
    data_regional_lgi,
    data_regional_psy,
    by = join_by(bblid),
    relationship = "many-to-many"
  ) |>
  drop_na()

test_lgi_psy_regional <-
  data_lgi_psy_regional |>
  summarize(
    lm(psychosis ~ regional_lgi) |>
      tidy(conf.int = TRUE) |>
      clean_names() |>
      filter(term == "regional_lgi"),
    .by = c(factor, region)
  ) |>
  separate(region, into = c("region", "laterality"), sep = "_") |>
  rename(b = estimate, p = p_value) |>
  mutate(
    region = roi_mapping[region],
    laterality = str_to_title(laterality),
    ci = sprintf("[%.3f, %.3f]", conf_low, conf_high)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    p_fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "fdr"),
    significance = case_when(
      p_fdr < 0.001 ~ "***",
      p_fdr < 0.01 ~ "**",
      p_fdr < 0.05 ~ "*",
      TRUE ~ ""
    ),
    .by = factor
  )

test_lgi_psy_regional |>
  select(region, laterality, factor, b, ci, p, p_fdr, significance) |>
  arrange(region, laterality, desc(factor)) |>
  kbl(
    col.names = c("Region", "Laterality", "Clinical Factor", "b", "95% CI", "p", "pFDR", ""),
    align = "llrrrrl",
    digits = c(NA, NA, NA, 3, NA, 5, 5, NA)
  )
```

:::

### Lobular LGI vs Psychosis Factor

At the lobe level in the full sample, after regressing `s(age) + sex` out of lobular LGI and psychosis factors, no lobes were found where LGI was significantly associated with psychosis.

::: {.collapsible-table data-rows="5"}

```{r}
#| label: lgi-psy-lobular-factor
#| test: {method: lm, dv: [psychosis positive, psychosis negative], iv: lgi}
#| control: {method: residual, variables: [age, sex]}
#| scale: lobe
plot_lgi_lobe <-
  ggplot(
    data = lgi_lobe,
    mapping = aes(x = lobe, y = lgi)
  ) +
  geom_boxplot() +

plot_lgi_lobe

data_lobular_lgi <-

data_lobular_psy <-

      ) |>

    by = join_by(bblid),

  ) |>

data_lgi_psy_lobular <-

test_lgi_psy_lobular <-

test_lgi_psy_lobular |>
```

### LGI Factors vs Psychosis Factor

An initial scree plot of regional LGI measures revealed a dominant first factor, suggesting substantial shared variance across cortical regions. To investigate additional regional variation, global LGI was regressed out of each regional LGI measure, and a second scree plot was generated from the residuals to guide the selection of regional factors. An exploratory bifactor model was then fitted to the original regional LGI measures, consisting of one general factor and eight specific regional factors. Bifactor indices, including factor determinacy (FD), were calculated to assess the suitability of the resulting factor scores for subsequent analyses. Only the general factor demonstrated adequate determinacy (FD = 0.995), while all eight regional factors fell below the selected threshold of FD ≥ 0.80 (range: 0.579–0.764). Consequently, the regional factor scores were not retained for downstream analyses.

```{r}
#| label: lgi-factor-analysis
#| control: {method: residual, variables: [age, sex]}
imaging_wide <-
  imaging |>
  mutate(region = str_c(region, laterality, sep = "_")) |>
  select(bblid, region, lgi) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = region, values_from = lgi) |>
  inner_join(
    demo |>
      select(bblid, age, sex),
    by = join_by(bblid),
    relationship = "one-to-one"
  ) |>
  drop_na() |>
  mutate(across(
    c(ends_with("_left"), ends_with("_right")),
    \(x) residuals(gam(x ~ s(age) + sex))
  )) |>
  select(-age, -sex)

scree(select(imaging_wide, -bblid), factors = TRUE)

regional_lgi_residuals <-
  imaging |>
  mutate(region = str_c(region, laterality, sep = "_")) |>
  select(bblid, region, lgi) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = region, values_from = lgi) |>
  inner_join(
    demo |>
      select(bblid, age, sex),
    by = join_by(bblid),
    relationship = "one-to-one"
  ) |>
  inner_join(
    global_lgi |>
      rename(global_lgi = lgi) |>
      select(bblid, global_lgi),
    by = join_by(bblid),
    relationship = "one-to-one"
  ) |>
  drop_na() |>
  mutate(across(
    c(ends_with("_left"), ends_with("_right")),
    \(x) residuals(gam(x ~ s(age) + s(global_lgi) + sex))
  )) |>
  select(-age, -sex, -global_lgi)

scree(select(regional_lgi_residuals, -bblid), factors = TRUE)

n_factors <- 9

fa_lgi <-
  fa(
    select(imaging_wide, -bblid),
    nfactors = n_factors,
    fm = "minres",
    rotate = "bifactor",
    scores = "regression"
  ) |>
  fa.organize(
    cn = c("Global", str_c("Region", 1:(n_factors - 1), sep = " "))
  )

colnames(fa_lgi$scores) <- colnames(fa_lgi$loadings)

invisible(capture.output(
  bifactor_indices <- bifactorIndices_expl(fa_lgi)
))

bifactor_indices |>
  pluck("FactorLevelIndices") |>
  rownames_to_column(var = "Factor") |>
  as_tibble() |>
  unnest(cols = everything()) |>
  select(Factor, FD) |>
  kbl()

loadings_lgi <- fa_lgi$loadings |>
  unclass() |>
  as_tibble(rownames = "roi") |>
  pivot_longer(
    -roi,
    names_to = "factor",
    values_to = "loading"
  ) |>
  separate(
    roi,
    into = c("region", "hemi"),
    sep = "_(?=[^_]+$)"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    region = str_replace_all(region, ggseg_mapping),
    factor = factor(factor)
  )

plot_loadings <- ggplot() +
  geom_brain(
    atlas = dk(),
    data = loadings_lgi |>
      filter(factor != "Global") |>
      group_by(factor),
    mapping = aes(fill = loading),
    position = position_brain(view ~ hemi)
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ factor, ncol = 4, nrow = 2) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = my_red,
    mid = "white",
    high = my_green,
    midpoint = 0,
    limits = c(-1, 1)
  ) +
  theme_void()

plot_loadings
```

### Differences in Regional LGI between Psychosis and TD

LGI is significantly lower in those with psychosis, relative to controls, in all regions other than the Left Inferior Temporal. Cohen's d, the standardized mean difference, varried widely, from relatively small $(d = 0.148)$ in the Left Lateral Occipital, to relatively large $(d = 0.375)$ in the Right Paracentral.

::: {.collapsible-table data-rows="5"}

```{r}
#| label: lgi-psy-regional-goa
#| test: {method: t-test, variable: lgi, groups: [dxpmrv7_td, dxpmrv7_ps]}
#| control: {method: residual, variables: [age, sex]}
#| scale: region
data_regional_td_psy <-
  inner_join(imaging, demo, by = join_by(bblid, scanid), relationship = "many-to-one") |>
  filter(dx %in% c("TD", "PS")) |>
  mutate(
    dx = fct_drop(dx),
    region = str_c(region, laterality, sep = "_")
  ) |>
  drop_na(bblid, scanid, region, lgi, dx, age, sex) |>
  mutate(lgi = residuals(gam(lgi ~ s(age) + sex)), .by = region) |>
  select(bblid, scanid, region, lgi, dx)

test_regional_psy <-
  data_regional_td_psy |>
  summarize(
    t.test(lgi ~ dx) |>
      tidy() |>
      clean_names(),
    cohens_d = cohens_d(lgi ~ dx)$Cohens_d,
    .by = region
  ) |>
  separate(region, into = c("region", "laterality"), sep = "_") |>
  rename(
    mean_difference = estimate,
    t = statistic,
    p = p_value
  ) |>
  mutate(
    region = roi_mapping[region],
    laterality = str_to_title(laterality),
    ci = sprintf("[%.3f, %.3f]", conf_low, conf_high),
    p_fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "fdr"),
    significance = case_when(
      p_fdr < 0.001 ~ "***",
      p_fdr < 0.01 ~ "**",
      p_fdr < 0.05 ~ "*",
      TRUE ~ ""
    )
  )

test_regional_psy |>
  select(region, laterality, mean_difference, ci, cohens_d, t, p, p_fdr, significance) |>
  kbl(
    col.names = c("Region", "Laterality", "Mean Difference", "95% CI", "Cohen's d", "t", "p", "pFDR", ""),
    align = "llrrrrrrl",
    digits = c(NA, NA, 3, NA, 3, 3, 5, 5, NA)
  )

plot_regional_psy <-
  ggplot() +
  geom_brain(
    atlas = dk(),
    data = test_regional_psy |>
      mutate(
        region = str_replace_all(
          setNames(names(roi_mapping), roi_mapping)[region],
          ggseg_mapping
        ),
        hemi = str_to_lower(laterality),
        cohens_d = replace_when(cohens_d, p_fdr >= 0.05 ~ NA)
      ),
    mapping = aes(fill = cohens_d),
    position = position_brain(view ~ hemi)
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() +
  labs(
    title = "Standardized Differences in Mean LGI Between TD and PS",
    caption = "Only differences with pFDR < 0.05 are shown.",
    fill = "Cohen's d"
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0))

plot_regional_psy
```

:::

# Psychopathology (Factor Scores)

General Psychopathology, Depression, and Psychosis Positive all showed a significant negative correlation with Global LGI. No such relationship was observed for ADHD, Mania or Psychosis Negative.

```{r}
#| label: clinical-factors-raw
#| test: {method: correlation, variables: [lgi, [general p, adhd, depression, mania, psychosis positive, psychosis negative]]}
#| control: {method: residual, variables: [age, sex]}
#| scale: global
data_lgi_clinical <-
  demo |>
  inner_join(global_lgi, by = join_by(bblid, scanid), relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  inner_join(clinical, by = join_by(bblid), relationship = "one-to-many") |>
  rename(clinical = value) |>
  filter(type == "bifactor") |>
  drop_na(bblid, scanid, lgi, factor, clinical, age, sex) |>
  mutate(
    lgi = residuals(gam(lgi ~ s(age) + sex)),
    clinical = residuals(gam(clinical ~ s(age) + sex)),
    .by = factor
  ) |>
  select(bblid, scanid, lgi, factor, clinical)

test_lgi_clinical <- data_lgi_clinical |>
  summarize(
    cor.test(lgi, clinical) |>
      tidy() |>
      clean_names(),
    .by = factor
  ) |>
  rename(
    r = estimate,
    p = p_value
  ) |>
  mutate(
    ci = sprintf("[%.3f, %.3f]", conf_low, conf_high),
    p_fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "fdr"),
    significance = case_when(
      p_fdr < 0.001 ~ "***",
      p_fdr < 0.01 ~ "**",
      p_fdr < 0.05 ~ "*",
      TRUE ~ ""
    )
  )

test_lgi_clinical |>
  select(factor, r, ci, p, p_fdr, significance) |>
  arrange(factor) |>
  kbl(
    col.names = c("Clinical Factor", "r", "95% CI", "p", "pFDR", ""),
    align = "lrrrrl",
    digits = c(NA, 3, NA, 5, 5, NA),
    caption = "Relationship Between Global LGI and Psychopathology Factors",
  )

labeller_lgi_clinical <-
  test_lgi_clinical |>
  mutate(label = str_trim(str_c(factor, significance, sep = " "))) |>
  select(factor, label) |>
  deframe() |>
  as_labeller()

plot_lgi_clinical <-
  ggplot(
    data = data_lgi_clinical,
    mapping = aes(x = lgi, y = clinical)
  ) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.25, size = 0.25) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm",
    formula = y ~ x,
    se = TRUE,
    color = "black",
    fill = "black",
    linewidth = 0.75,
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ factor, labeller = labeller_lgi_clinical) +
  labs(
    title = "Relationship Between Global LGI and Psychopathology Factors",
    x = "Global LGI",
    y = "Psychopathology"
  ) +
  theme_linedraw()

plot_lgi_clinical
```

# Psychopathology (Binary GOASSESS)

Participants with anxiety disorders, behavioral disorders, eating disorders, mood disorders, and psychotic disorders all had significantly lower global LGI than participants without such disorders.

## Differences in Global LGI Between GOASSESS Categories

```{r}
#| label: lgi-goa-cat
#| test: {method: t-test, variable: lgi, group across: smry_cat_*}
#| control: {method: residual, variables: [age, sex]}
#| scale: global
data_lgi_goa_cat <-
  inner_join(demo, global_lgi, by = join_by(bblid, scanid), relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  inner_join(goassess_category, by = join_by(bblid), relationship = "one-to-many") |>
  drop_na(bblid, scanid, lgi, category, status, age, sex) |>
  mutate(lgi = residuals(gam(lgi ~ s(age) + sex)), .by = category) |>

test_lgi_goa_cat <-
  data_lgi_goa_cat |>
  summarize(
    n_true = sum(status),
    n_false = sum(!status),
    t.test(lgi ~ status) |>
      tidy() |>
      clean_names(),
    cohens_d = cohens_d(lgi ~ status)$Cohens_d,
    .by = category
  ) |>
  transmute(
    category,
    n_true,
    n_false,
    mean_difference = estimate,
    ci = sprintf("[%.3f, %.3f]", conf_low, conf_high),
    cohens_d,
    t = statistic,
    p = p_value,
    p_fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "fdr"),
    significance = case_when(
      p_fdr < 0.001 ~ "***",
      p_fdr < 0.01 ~ "**",
      p_fdr < 0.05 ~ "*",
      TRUE ~ ""
    )
  )

test_lgi_goa_cat |>
  arrange(category) |>
  kbl(
    col.names = c("Category", "n True", "n False", "Mean Difference", "95% CI", "Cohen's d", "t", "p", "pFDR", ""),
    align = "lrrrrrrrrl",
    digits = c(NA, 0, 0, 3, NA, 3, 3, 5, 5, NA)
  )

summary_lgi_goa_cat <-
  data_lgi_goa_cat |>
  summarize(
    n = n(),
    fit = mean(lgi),
    se = sd(lgi) / sqrt(n),
    lower = fit - qt(0.975, df = n - 1) * se,
    upper = fit + qt(0.975, df = n - 1) * se,
    .by = c(category, status)
  )

labels_lgi_goa_cat <-
  test_lgi_goa_cat |>
  mutate(label = str_trim(str_c(category, significance, sep = " "))) |>
  select(category, label) |>
  deframe() |>
  as_labeller()

plot_lgi_goa_cat <-
  ggplot() +
  geom_jitter(
    data = data_lgi_goa_cat,
    mapping = aes(x = as.numeric(status), y = lgi, color = status, fill = status),

    size = 0.25
  ) +
  geom_rect(
    data = summary_lgi_goa_cat,

      xmin = status - 0.4,
      xmax = status + 0.4,
      ymin = lower,
      ymax = upper,
      fill = status
    ),
    alpha = 0.5,
    color = NA
  ) +
  geom_segment(
    data = summary_lgi_goa_cat,
    mapping = aes(
      x = status - 0.4,
      xend = status + 0.4,
      y = fit,
      yend = fit,
      color = status
    ),
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ category, labeller = labels_lgi_goa_cat) +
  color_scale_dx +

  labs(
    title = "Differences in Global LGI across GOASSESS Categories",

    color = "Status",
    fill = "Status"
```

# Cognition

## Association of CNB Accuracy and Global LGI

### Full Sample

In the full sample, Global LGI is significantly positvely associated with cognitive efficiency in the following domains when controlling for eTIV and after correcting for multiple comparisons: Overall Cognition, Complex Cognition, Motor, Social Cognition. Global LGI was significantly positively associated with Memory Efficiency but this effect did not survive correcting for eTIV.

```{r}
#| label: lgi-cnb-full-sample
#| test: {method: lm, dv: [overall, executive, memory, complex, social], iv: lgi}
#| control: {method: residual, variables: [age, sex]}
#| sample: full sample
#| scale: global
#| cnb-metric: accuracy
data_lgi_cnb <-
  cnb |>
  inner_join(global_lgi, by = join_by(bblid, scanid), relationship = "many-to-one") |>
  inner_join(demo, by = join_by(bblid, scanid), relationship = "many-to-one") |>
  rename(cnb = value) |>
  filter(measure %in% c("Accuracy", "Speed")) |>
  drop_na() |>
  mutate(
    lgi = residuals(gam(lgi ~ s(age) + sex)),
    cnb = residuals(gam(cnb ~ sex)),
    .by = c(domain, measure)
  ) |>
  select(bblid, scanid, domain, measure, cnb, lgi)

test_lgi_cnb <-
  data_lgi_cnb |>
  summarize(
    lm(cnb ~ lgi) |>
      tidy(conf.int = TRUE) |>
      clean_names() |>
      filter(term == "lgi"),
    .by = c(domain, measure)
  ) |>
  rename(b = estimate, p = p_value) |>
  mutate(
    ci = sprintf("[%.3f, %.3f]", conf_low, conf_high),
    p_fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "fdr"),
    significance = case_when(
      p_fdr < 0.001 ~ "***",
      p_fdr < 0.01 ~ "**",
      p_fdr < 0.05 ~ "*",
      TRUE ~ ""
    ),
    .by = measure
  )

test_lgi_cnb |>
  filter(measure == "Accuracy") |>
  select(domain, b, ci, p, p_fdr, significance) |>
  arrange(domain) |>
  kbl(
    col.names = c("Domain", "b", "95% CI", "p", "pFDR", ""),
    align = "lrrrrl",
    digits = c(NA, 3, NA, 5, 5, NA),
    caption = "Association of CNB Accuracy with Global LGI"
  )

facet_labels_lgi_cnb_acc <-
  test_lgi_cnb |>
  filter(measure == "Accuracy") |>
  mutate(label = str_trim(str_c(domain, significance, sep = " "))) |>
  select(domain, label) |>
  deframe() |>
  as_labeller()

plot_lgi_cnb_acc <-
  ggplot(
    data = data_lgi_cnb |> filter(measure == "Accuracy"),
    mapping = aes(x = lgi, y = cnb)
  ) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.1, size = 1) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm",
    formula = y ~ x,
    se = TRUE,
    color = "black",
    fill = "black",
    linewidth = 0.75,
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ domain, labeller = facet_labels_lgi_cnb_acc) +
  labs(
    title = "Relationship Between Global LGI and CNB Accuracy",
    x = "Global LGI",
    y = "Accuracy"
  ) +
  theme_linedraw()

plot_lgi_cnb_acc

test_lgi_cnb |>
  filter(measure == "Speed") |>
  select(domain, b, ci, p, p_fdr, significance) |>
  arrange(domain) |>
  kbl(
    col.names = c("Domain", "b", "95% CI", "p", "pFDR", ""),
    align = "lrrrrl",
    digits = c(NA, 3, NA, 5, 5, NA),
    caption = "Association of CNB Speed with Global LGI"
  )

facet_labels_lgi_cnb_spd <-
  test_lgi_cnb |>
  filter(measure == "Speed") |>
  mutate(label = str_trim(str_c(domain, significance, sep = " "))) |>
  select(domain, label) |>
  deframe() |>
  as_labeller()

plot_lgi_cnb_spd <-
  ggplot(
    data = data_lgi_cnb |> filter(measure == "Speed"),
    mapping = aes(x = lgi, y = cnb)
  ) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.1, size = 1) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm",
    formula = y ~ x,
    se = TRUE,
    color = "black",
    fill = "black",
    linewidth = 0.75,
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ domain, labeller = facet_labels_lgi_cnb_spd) +
  labs(
    title = "Relationship Between Global LGI and CNB Speed",
    x = "Global LGI",
    y = "Speed"
  ) +
  theme_linedraw()

plot_lgi_cnb_spd
```

### Clean Subsample

In the Clean Subsample, Global LGI is significantly positively associated with Motor Efficiency. This effect survives multiple comparison correction but is no longer significant when controlling for eTIV.

```{r}
#| label: lgi-cnb-clean-subsample
#| test: {method: lm, dv: [overall, executive, memory, complex, social], iv: lgi}
#| control: {method: residual, variables: [age, sex]}
#| sample: clean subsample
#| scale: global
#| cnb-metric: accuracy
data_lgi_cnb_clean <-
  cnb |>
  inner_join(global_lgi, by = join_by(bblid, scanid), relationship = "many-to-one") |>
  inner_join(demo, by = join_by(bblid, scanid), relationship = "many-to-one") |>
  semi_join(clean_subsample, by = join_by(bblid)) |>
  rename(cnb = value) |>
  filter(measure %in% c("Accuracy", "Speed")) |>
  drop_na() |>
  mutate(
    lgi = residuals(gam(lgi ~ s(age) + sex)),
    cnb = residuals(gam(cnb ~ sex)),
    .by = c(domain, measure)
  ) |>
  select(bblid, scanid, domain, measure, cnb, lgi)

test_lgi_cnb_clean <-
  data_lgi_cnb_clean |>
  summarize(
    lm(cnb ~ lgi) |>
      tidy(conf.int = TRUE) |>
      clean_names() |>
      filter(term == "lgi"),
    .by = c(domain, measure)
  ) |>
  rename(b = estimate, p = p_value) |>
  mutate(
    ci = sprintf("[%.3f, %.3f]", conf_low, conf_high),
    p_fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "fdr"),
    significance = case_when(
      p_fdr < 0.001 ~ "***",
      p_fdr < 0.01 ~ "**",
      p_fdr < 0.05 ~ "*",
      TRUE ~ ""
    ),
    .by = measure
  )

test_lgi_cnb_clean |>
  select(measure, domain, b, ci, p, p_fdr, significance) |>
  arrange(measure, domain) |>
  kbl(
    col.names = c("Measure", "Domain", "b", "95% CI", "p", "pFDR", ""),
    align = "llrrrrl",
    digits = c(NA, NA, 3, NA, 5, 5, NA),
    caption = "Association of CNB Performance with Global LGI"
  )
```

## Cognitive Profile of LGI-Volume Tertile Groups

```{r}
#| label: cnb-profiles
#| test: {method: anova, dv: [overall, executive, memory, complex, social], groups: lgi-volume tertile groups}
#| control: {method: residual, variables: [age, sex], sample: full sample}
#| sample: tertile groups
#| scale: global
#| cnb-metric: [accuracy, speed]
groups <- c("g1v1", "g3v1", "g1v3", "g3v3")

data_tertile_cnb <-
  data_lgi_cnb |>
  inner_join(
    data_lgi_vol_tertile |>
      select(bblid, group),
    by = join_by(bblid),
    relationship = "many-to-one"
  ) |>
  filter(group %in% groups) |>
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = groups))

test_tertile_cnb <-
  data_tertile_cnb |>
  summarize(model = list(aov(cnb ~ group)), .by = c(domain, measure))

result_tertile_cnb <-
  test_tertile_cnb |>
  mutate(
    list_rbind(
      map(model, \(m) {
        m |>
        tidy() |>
        clean_names() |>
        filter(term == "group")
      })
    ),
    df_residual = map_dbl(model, df.residual),
    eta2 = map_dbl(model, \(m) {
      t <- tidy(m)
      t$sumsq[t$term == "group"] / sum(t$sumsq)
    })
  ) |>
  rename(
    f = statistic,
    df1 = df,
    df2 = df_residual,
    p = p_value,
  ) |>
  mutate(
    p_fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "fdr"),
    significance = case_when(
      p_fdr < 0.001 ~ "***",
      p_fdr < 0.01 ~ "**",
      p_fdr < 0.05 ~ "*",
      TRUE ~ ""
    ),
    .by = measure
  ) |>
  select(
    measure, domain,
    f, df1, df2, eta2,
    p, p_fdr, significance,
  )

posthoc_tertile_cnb <-
  test_tertile_cnb |>
  mutate(
    posthoc = map(model, \(m) m |> TukeyHSD() |> tidy() |> clean_names()),
    sigma = map_dbl(model, sigma)
  ) |>
  select(domain, measure, posthoc, sigma) |>
  unnest(posthoc) |>
  rename(
    mean_difference = estimate,
    p_tukey = adj_p_value,
  ) |>
  mutate(
    ci = sprintf("[%.3f, %.3f]", conf_low, conf_high),
    cohens_d = mean_difference / sigma,
    significance = case_when(
      p_tukey < 0.001 ~ "***",
      p_tukey < 0.01 ~ "**",
      p_tukey < 0.05 ~ "*",
      TRUE ~ ""
    )
  ) |>
  separate(
    contrast,
    into = c("group1", "group2"),
    sep = "-",
    remove = FALSE
  ) |>
  select(domain, measure, contrast, mean_difference, ci, cohens_d, p_tukey, significance, group1, group2)

summary_tertile_cnb <-
  data_tertile_cnb |>
  summarize(
    n = n(),
    mean = mean(cnb),
    se = sd(cnb) / sqrt(n),
    lower = mean - qt(0.975, df = n - 1) * se,
    upper = mean + qt(0.975, df = n - 1) * se,
    .by = c(domain, measure, group)
  )

sig_tertile_cnb <-
  posthoc_tertile_cnb |>
  filter(p_tukey < 0.05) |>
  left_join(
    summary_tertile_cnb |>
      select(domain, measure, group, mean) |>
      rename(group1 = group, y1 = mean),
    by = join_by(domain, group1, measure),
    relationship = "many-to-one"
  ) |>
  left_join(
    summary_tertile_cnb |>
      select(domain, measure, group, mean) |>
      rename(group2 = group, y2 = mean),
    by = join_by(domain, group2, measure),
    relationship = "many-to-one"
  ) |>
  group_by(domain, measure) |>
  arrange(p_tukey, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  mutate(
    x = as.numeric(domain) +
      0.065 * (row_number() - (n() + 1) / 2),
    ymin = pmin(y1, y2),
    ymax = pmax(y1, y2)
  ) |>
  ungroup()
```

```{r}
#| label: cnb-profiles-accuracy

ggplot(

    caption = "Tukey's HSD post-hoc comparisons between LGI/volume groups within each cognitive domain. Results include mean differences, 95% confidence intervals, Cohen's d, and Tukey-adjusted p-values. Adjustments were performed separately within each domain."
  )

ggplot(
    data = summary_tertile_cnb |>
      filter(measure == "Accuracy"),

    )

  geom_point() +
  geom_segment(
    data = sig_tertile_cnb |>
      filter(measure == "Accuracy"),
    aes(x = x, xend = x, y = ymin, yend = ymax),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    color = "black"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq_along(levels(summary_tertile_cnb$domain)),

  ) +
```

```{r}
    col.names = c("Domain", "Contrast", "Mean Difference", "95% CI", "Cohen's d", "p Tukey", ""),
    align = "llrrrrl",
    digits = c(NA, NA, 3, NA, 3, 5, NA),
    caption = "Tukey's HSD post-hoc comparisons between LGI/volume groups within each cognitive domain. Results include mean differences, 95% confidence intervals, Cohen's d, and Tukey-adjusted p-values. Adjustments were performed separately within each domain."
  )

ggplot(
    data = summary_tertile_cnb |>
      filter(measure == "Speed"),
    mapping = aes(
      x = as.numeric(domain),
      y = mean, ymin = lower, ymax = upper,
      group = group, color = group, fill = group
    )
  ) +
  geom_ribbon(alpha = 0.25, color = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  geom_segment(
    data = sig_tertile_cnb |>
      filter(measure == "Speed"),
    aes(x = x, xend = x, y = ymin, yend = ymax),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    color = "black"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq_along(levels(summary_tertile_cnb$domain)),
    labels = labels_tertile_cnb_spd[levels(summary_tertile_cnb$domain)]
  ) +
  color_scale_group +
  fill_scale_group +
  labs(
    x = "Domain",
    y = "Speed"
  ) +
  theme_linedraw()
```

:::

# Main Effects

  - Global LGI declined nonlinearly with age, with a modest departure from linearity. [`lgi ~ s(age)`](#main-age)
  - Global LGI was positively and linearly associated with SES, with no evidence of significant nonlinearity. [`lgi ~ ses`](#main-ses)
  - Global LGI was significantly higher in males than females (p < 0.001). [`lgi ~ sex`](#main-sex)
  - Global LGI declined with increasing trauma exposure, with evidence of modest nonlinearity in the relationship. [`lgi ~ s(trauma, k = 7)`](#main-trauma)

## Global LGI ~ Age {#main-age}

Global LGI was significantly negatively associated with age, with evidence that this relationship was nonlinear, although the nonlinearity was relatively subtle. The nonlinear age model was favored over the linear model based on AIC and the significance of the additional nonlinear component. In the final model, age was significantly associated with global LGI (edf = 3.232, p < 0.001), explaining approximately 31.5% of the deviance. Model diagnostics indicated satisfactory convergence and no evidence of an insufficient basis dimension (k-index = 1.01, p = 0.64). The final model was therefore lgi ~ s(age).

::: {.content-visible when-profile="scratch"}

### Sample

```{r}
#| label: lgi-age-data
data_lgi_age <-
  inner_join(global_lgi, demo, by = join_by(bblid), relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  select(lgi, age) |>
  drop_na()
```

### Model Selection

#### Model 1: Linear Age Effect

This model tests whether age has a significant linear association with global LGI. Age was a significant predictor, with increasing age associated with lower global LGI. The model explained approximately 31.0% of the deviance.

```{r}
#| label: lgi-age-1
model_lgi_age_1 <- gam(
  lgi ~ age,
  data = data_lgi_age,
  method = "ML"
)

summary(model_lgi_age_1)
```

#### Model 2: Linear and Nonlinear Age Effects

This model tests whether age has significant linear and nonlinear associations with global LGI. Both the linear and nonlinear components of age were significant, with increasing age associated with lower global LGI. The nonlinear component was significant (p = 0.0115, edf = 1.559), suggesting that the relationship between age and LGI deviates modestly from linearity.

```{r}
#| label: lgi-age-2
model_lgi_age_2 <- gam(
  lgi ~ age + s(age, m = c(2, 0)),
  data = data_lgi_age,
  method = "ML"
)

summary(model_lgi_age_2)
```

#### AIC

Model 2 had a lower AIC than Model 1 (ΔAIC = 4.19), indicating greater support for a nonlinear age association. The significant nonlinear component in Model 2 further suggested that allowing curvature improved the representation of the age–LGI relationship. A nonlinear age specification was therefore selected and implemented as lgi ~ s(age) for the final model, which was refitted using REML.

```{r}
#| label: lgi-age-selection
aic_lgi_age <- report_aic(list(
  model_lgi_age_1 = model_lgi_age_1,
  model_lgi_age_2 = model_lgi_age_2
))

aic_lgi_age |>
  kbl(
    col.names = c("", "Formula", "df", "AIC", "ΔAIC"),
    digits = 2
  )
```

#### Check Final Model

```{r}
#| label: lgi-age-final
model_lgi_age_final <- gam(
  lgi ~ s(age),
  data = data_lgi_age,
  method = "REML"
)

gam.check(model_lgi_age_final)
```

### Results

:::

```{r}
#| label: lgi-age-results
summary(model_lgi_age_final)

prediction_lgi_age <- data_lgi_age |>
  summarise(
    age = list(
      seq(
        min(age, na.rm = TRUE),
        max(age, na.rm = TRUE),
        length.out = 250
      )
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  unnest(age)

fit_lgi_age <-
  predict(
    model_lgi_age_final,
    newdata = prediction_lgi_age,
    type = "response",
    se.fit = TRUE
  ) |>
  map(as.vector) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  clean_names() |>
  mutate(lower = fit - 1.96 * se_fit, upper = fit + 1.96 * se_fit) |>
  select(fit, lower, upper)

prediction_lgi_age <- prediction_lgi_age |>
  bind_cols(fit_lgi_age)

plot_lgi_age <-
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = age, y = lgi)) +
  geom_point(data = data_lgi_age, alpha = 0.25, size = 1) +
  geom_ribbon(
    data = prediction_lgi_age,
    mapping = aes(y = fit, ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
    alpha = 0.5,
    color = NA
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = prediction_lgi_age,
    mapping = aes(y = fit),
    linewidth = 0.75
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "LGI Developmental Trajectory",
    x = "Age",
    y = "LGI (global)"
  ) +
  theme_linedraw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

plot_lgi_age
```

## Global LGI ~ SES {#main-ses}

Global LGI was significantly positively associated with SES, with higher SES associated with higher global LGI. There was insufficient evidence of a nonlinear association, as the nonlinear component was not statistically significant and was effectively penalized to zero. The linear model was selected based on AIC and parsimony. In the final model, SES was significantly associated with global LGI (β = 0.0314, p < 0.001), explaining approximately 4.26% of the deviance. Model diagnostics indicated satisfactory convergence. The final model was therefore lgi ~ ses.

::: {.content-visible when-profile="scratch"}

### Sample

```{r}
#| label: lgi-ses-data
data_lgi_ses <-
  inner_join(global_lgi, env, by = join_by(bblid), relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  select(lgi, ses) |>
  drop_na()
```

### Model Selection

#### Model 1: Linear SES Effect

This model tests whether SES has a significant linear association with global LGI. SES was a significant predictor, with higher SES associated with higher global LGI. The model explained approximately 4.26% of the deviance.

```{r}
#| label: lgi-ses-1
model_lgi_ses_1 <- gam(
  lgi ~ ses,
  data = data_lgi_ses,
  method = "ML"
)

summary(model_lgi_ses_1)
```

#### Model 2: Linear and Nonlinear SES Effects

This model tests whether SES has significant linear and nonlinear associations with global LGI. The linear component of SES was significant, with higher SES associated with higher global LGI. The nonlinear component was not significant (p = 0.222) and was effectively penalized to zero (edf = 0.0001), suggesting an approximately linear relationship between SES and LGI.

```{r}
#| label: lgi-ses-2
model_lgi_ses_2 <- gam(
  lgi ~ ses + s(ses, m = c(2, 0)),
  data = data_lgi_ses,
  method = "ML"
)

summary(model_lgi_ses_2)
```

#### AIC

Both models exhibited nearly identical AIC values (ΔAIC < 0.001), indicating comparable model support. Model 1 had the lowest AIC, while Model 2 had a nearly identical AIC, consistent with its nonlinear SES component being effectively penalized to zero. Model 1 was therefore selected on the basis of AIC and parsimony, retaining a linear effect of SES without an additional nonlinear component.

```{r}
#| label: lgi-ses-selection
aic_lgi_ses <- report_aic(list(
  model_lgi_ses_1 = model_lgi_ses_1,
  model_lgi_ses_2 = model_lgi_ses_2
))

aic_lgi_ses |>
  kbl(
    col.names = c("", "Formula", "df", "AIC", "ΔAIC"),
    digits = 2
  )
```

#### Check Final Model

```{r}
#| label: lgi-ses-final
model_lgi_ses_final <- gam(
  lgi ~ ses,
  data = data_lgi_ses,
  method = "REML"
)

gam.check(model_lgi_ses_final)
```

### Results

:::

```{r}
#| label: lgi-ses-results
summary(model_lgi_ses_final)

prediction_lgi_ses <- data_lgi_ses |>
  summarise(
    ses = list(
      seq(
        min(ses, na.rm = TRUE),
        max(ses, na.rm = TRUE),
        length.out = 250
      )
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  unnest(ses)

fit_lgi_ses <-
  predict(
    model_lgi_ses_final,
    newdata = prediction_lgi_ses,
    type = "response",
    se.fit = TRUE
  ) |>
  map(as.vector) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  clean_names() |>
  mutate(lower = fit - 1.96 * se_fit, upper = fit + 1.96 * se_fit) |>
  select(fit, lower, upper)

prediction_lgi_ses <- prediction_lgi_ses |>
  bind_cols(fit_lgi_ses)

plot_lgi_ses <-
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = ses, y = lgi)) +
  geom_point(data = data_lgi_ses, alpha = 0.25, size = 1) +
  geom_ribbon(
    data = prediction_lgi_ses,
    mapping = aes(y = fit, ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
    alpha = 0.5,
    color = NA
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = prediction_lgi_ses,
    mapping = aes(y = fit),
    linewidth = 0.75
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "LGI SES Relationship",
    x = "SES",
    y = "LGI (global)"
  ) +
  theme_linedraw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

plot_lgi_ses
```

## Global LGI ~ Sex {#main-sex}

Global LGI differed significantly between sexes, with males exhibiting higher global LGI than females (β = 0.1091, p < 0.001). Sex explained approximately 11.9% of the deviance in global LGI. Model diagnostics indicated satisfactory convergence. The final model was therefore `lgi ~ sex`.

::: {.content-visible when-profile="scratch"}

### Sample

```{r}
#| label: lgi-sex-data
data_lgi_sex <-

```

```{r}
  data = data_lgi_sex,
```


## Global LGI ~ Trauma {#main-trauma}

Global LGI was significantly negatively associated with trauma exposure, with evidence that this relationship was nonlinear. The nonlinear trauma model was favored over the linear model based on AIC and the significance of the additional nonlinear component, although the improvement in model fit was relatively small. In the final model, trauma exposure was significantly associated with global LGI (edf = 2.298, p < 0.001), explaining approximately 4.26% of the deviance. Model diagnostics indicated satisfactory convergence, although the low k-index (0.84, p < 0.001) suggested potential residual structure warranting further examination. The final model was therefore lgi ~ s(trauma, k = 7).

::: {.content-visible when-profile="scratch"}

### Sample

```{r}
#| label: lgi-trauma-data
data_lgi_trauma <-
  inner_join(global_lgi, env, by = join_by(bblid), relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  select(lgi, trauma) |>
  drop_na()
```

### Model Selection

#### Model 1: Linear Trauma Effect

This model tests whether trauma exposure has a significant linear association with global LGI. Trauma exposure was a significant predictor, with greater trauma exposure associated with lower global LGI. The model explained approximately 3.90% of the deviance.

```{r}
#| label: lgi-trauma-1
model_lgi_trauma_1 <- gam(
  lgi ~ trauma,
  data = data_lgi_trauma,
  method = "ML"
)

summary(model_lgi_trauma_1)
```

#### Model 2: Linear and Nonlinear Trauma Effects

This model tests whether trauma exposure has significant linear and nonlinear associations with global LGI. Both the linear and nonlinear components of trauma exposure were significant, with greater trauma exposure associated with lower global LGI. The nonlinear component was significant (p = 0.0304, edf = 0.640), suggesting that the relationship between trauma exposure and LGI deviates modestly from linearity.

```{r}
#| label: lgi-trauma-2
model_lgi_trauma_2 <- gam(
  lgi ~ trauma + s(trauma, k = 7, m = c(2, 0)),
  data = data_lgi_trauma,
  method = "ML"
)

summary(model_lgi_trauma_2)
```

#### AIC

Model 2 had a lower AIC than Model 1 (ΔAIC = 1.73), indicating a slight preference for the nonlinear model, although both models exhibited comparable support (ΔAIC < 2). The significant nonlinear component in Model 2 provided additional evidence that allowing curvature improved the representation of the trauma–LGI relationship. A nonlinear trauma specification was therefore selected and implemented as lgi ~ s(trauma, k = 7) for the final model, which was refitted using REML.

```{r}
#| label: lgi-trauma-selection
aic_lgi_trauma <- report_aic(list(
  model_lgi_trauma_1 = model_lgi_trauma_1,
  model_lgi_trauma_2 = model_lgi_trauma_2
))

aic_lgi_trauma |>
  kbl(
    col.names = c("", "Formula", "df", "AIC", "ΔAIC"),
    digits = 2
  )
```

#### Check Final Model

```{r}
#| label: lgi-trauma-final
model_lgi_trauma_final <- gam(
  lgi ~ s(trauma, k = 7),
  data = data_lgi_trauma,
  method = "REML"
)

gam.check(model_lgi_trauma_final)
```

### Results

:::

```{r}
#| label: lgi-trauma-results

prediction_lgi_trauma <- data_lgi_trauma |>
  summarise(
    trauma = list(
      seq(
        min(trauma, na.rm = TRUE),
        max(trauma, na.rm = TRUE),
        length.out = 250
      )
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  unnest(trauma)

fit_lgi_trauma <-

prediction_lgi_trauma <- prediction_lgi_trauma |>
```

# Two-Way Interactions

  - Global LGI was nonlinearly associated with age and positively associated with SES, with no evidence of either a linear or nonlinear age × SES interaction. [`lgi ~ s(age) + ses`](#two-age-ses)
  - Global LGI declined nonlinearly with age and was significantly higher in males than females, with no evidence of either a linear or nonlinear age × sex interaction. [`lgi ~ s(age) + sex`](#two-age-sex)
  - Global LGI was linearly associated with age and trauma exposure, with a significant linear age × trauma interaction but no evidence of additional nonlinearity. [`lgi ~ age * trauma`](#two-age-trauma)
  - Global LGI was positively and linearly associated with SES and was significantly higher in males than females, with no evidence of either a linear or nonlinear SES × sex interaction. [`lgi ~ ses + sex`](#two-ses-sex)
  - Global LGI was positively and linearly associated with SES and negatively and linearly associated with trauma exposure, with no evidence of either a linear or nonlinear SES × trauma interaction. [`lgi ~ ses + trauma`](#two-ses-trauma)
  - Global LGI was negatively and linearly associated with trauma exposure and was significantly higher in males than females, with no evidence of either a linear or nonlinear sex × trauma interaction. [`lgi ~ sex + trauma`](#two-sex-trauma)

## Global LGI ~ Age x SES {#two-age-ses}

Age and SES were not significantly correlated. When modeled together, age showed a significant nonlinear association with global LGI, while SES showed a significant linear association, suggesting that both contributed independently to LGI. There was no evidence of a significant linear age × SES interaction, and a more flexible tensor-product interaction was also not significant. The most complex model supported by the data was therefore `lgi ~ s(age) + ses`.

::: {.content-visible when-profile="scratch"}

### Sample

```{r}
#| label: lgi-age-ses-data
data_lgi_age_ses <-
  global_lgi |>
  inner_join(demo, by = join_by(bblid), relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  inner_join(env, by = join_by(bblid), relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  select(lgi, age, ses) |>
  drop_na() |>
  mutate(age_c = age - mean(age), ses_c = ses - mean(ses))
```

:::

### Predictor Association

```{r}
#| label: lgi-age-ses-test
test_age_ses <-
  cor.test(data_lgi_age_ses$age, data_lgi_age_ses$ses)

test_age_ses
```

::: {.content-visible when-profile="scratch"}

### Model Selection

#### Model 1: Additive Linear and Nonlinear Effects

This model tests whether age and SES have significant linear and nonlinear associations with global LGI. Both the linear and nonlinear components of age are significant, suggesting a nonlinear relationship between age and LGI. Only the linear component of SES is significant, suggesting a linear relationship between SES and LGI.

```{r}
#| label: lgi-age-ses-1
model_lgi_age_ses_1 <- gam(
  lgi ~ age +
    ses +
    s(age, m = c(2, 0)) +
    s(ses, m = c(2, 0)),
  data = data_lgi_age_ses,
  method = "ML"
)

summary(model_lgi_age_ses_1)
```

#### Model 2: Linear Interaction with Nonlinear Main Effects

This model tests whether a linear interaction between age and SES is significantly associated with global LGI while allowing nonlinear main effects of both predictors. The linear interaction was not significant, suggesting insufficient evidence of an interaction between age and SES. Both the linear and nonlinear components of age are significant, suggesting a nonlinear relationship between age and LGI. Only the linear component of SES is significant, suggesting a linear relationship between SES and LGI.

```{r}
#| label: lgi-age-ses-2
model_lgi_age_ses_2 <- gam(
  lgi ~ age_c * ses_c +
    s(age_c, m = c(2, 0)) +
    s(ses_c, m = c(2, 0)),
  data = data_lgi_age_ses,
  method = "ML"
)

summary(model_lgi_age_ses_2)
```

#### Model 3: Tensor Product Interaction with Nonlinear Main Effects

This model tests whether a potentially nonlinear interaction between age and SES is significantly associated with global LGI while allowing nonlinear main effects of both predictors. The interaction was not significant, suggesting insufficient evidence of an interaction between age and SES. The smooth effect of age was significant, suggesting a nonlinear relationship between age and LGI. The smooth effect of SES was significant (edf = 1.000), suggesting a linear relationship between SES and LGI.

```{r}
#| label: lgi-age-ses-3
model_lgi_age_ses_3 <- gam(
  lgi ~ s(age) +
    s(ses) +
    ti(age, ses),
  data = data_lgi_age_ses,
  method = "ML"
)

summary(model_lgi_age_ses_3)
```

#### Model 4: Additive Nonlinear Age Effect and Linear SES Effect

This model includes a nonlinear effect of age and a linear effect of SES on global LGI, without an interaction. Both the nonlinear age smooth and the linear SES term were statistically significant, suggesting that age has a nonlinear association with global LGI, whereas SES has a linear association.

```{r}
#| label: lgi-age-ses-4
model_lgi_age_ses_4 <- gam(
  lgi ~ age +
    ses +
    s(age, m = c(2, 0)),
  data = data_lgi_age_ses,
  method = "ML"
)

summary(model_lgi_age_ses_4)
```

#### AIC

All four models exhibited similar AIC values (ΔAIC < 2), indicating comparable model support. Although Model 2 had the lowest AIC, neither the linear nor tensor product interaction was statistically significant. Models 1 and 4 exhibited nearly identical AIC values, consistent with the nonlinear SES component in Model 1 being penalized effectively to zero. Model 4 was selected on the basis of parsimony, retaining a nonlinear effect of age and a linear effect of SES without an interaction.

```{r}
#| label: lgi-age-ses-selection
aic_lgi_age_ses <- report_aic(list(
  model_lgi_age_ses_1 = model_lgi_age_ses_1,
  model_lgi_age_ses_2 = model_lgi_age_ses_2,
  model_lgi_age_ses_3 = model_lgi_age_ses_3,
  model_lgi_age_ses_4 = model_lgi_age_ses_4
))

aic_lgi_age_ses |>
  kbl(
    col.names = c("", "Formula", "df", "AIC", "ΔAIC"),
    digits = 2
  )
```

#### Check Final Model

```{r}
#| label: lgi-age-ses-final
model_lgi_age_ses_final <- gam(
  lgi ~ s(age) + ses,
  data = data_lgi_age_ses,
  method = "REML"
)

gam.check(model_lgi_age_ses_final)
```

:::

### Results

```{r}
#| label: lgi-age-ses-results
summary(model_lgi_age_ses_final)

# LGI-Age by SES plot

ses_0 <- min(data_lgi_age_ses$ses, na.rm = TRUE)
ses_16 <- unname(quantile(data_lgi_age_ses$ses, probs = 1 / 6))
ses_33 <- unname(quantile(data_lgi_age_ses$ses, probs = 1 / 3))
ses_50 <- unname(quantile(data_lgi_age_ses$ses, probs = 1 / 2))
ses_66 <- unname(quantile(data_lgi_age_ses$ses, probs = 2 / 3))
ses_83 <- unname(quantile(data_lgi_age_ses$ses, probs = 5 / 6))
ses_100 <- max(data_lgi_age_ses$ses, na.rm = TRUE)

prediction_lgi_age_ses_1 <- data_lgi_age_ses |>
  mutate(
    ses = case_when(
      ses <= ses_33 ~ ses_16,
      ses > ses_33 & ses <= ses_66 ~ ses_50,
      ses > ses_66 ~ ses_83
    )
  ) |>
  summarise(
    age = list(
      seq(
        min(age, na.rm = TRUE),
        max(age, na.rm = TRUE),
        length.out = 250
      )
    ),
    .by = ses
  ) |>
  unnest(age)

fit_lgi_age_ses_1 <-
  predict(
    model_lgi_age_ses_final,
    newdata = prediction_lgi_age_ses_1,
    type = "response",
    se.fit = TRUE
  ) |>
  map(as.vector) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  clean_names() |>
  mutate(lower = fit - 1.96 * se_fit, upper = fit + 1.96 * se_fit) |>
  select(fit, lower, upper)

prediction_lgi_age_ses_1 <- prediction_lgi_age_ses_1 |>
  bind_cols(fit_lgi_age_ses_1)
```

## Global LGI ~ Age x Sex {#two-age-sex}

Age differed significantly by sex, with females being slightly older than males on average. When modeled together, global LGI showed a significant nonlinear association with age and a significant main effect of sex, with males exhibiting higher global LGI than females after accounting for age. Neither the linear nor nonlinear age × sex interaction was statistically significant, suggesting insufficient evidence that the relationship between age and global LGI differs by sex. The most complex model supported by the data was therefore `lgi ~ s(age) + sex`.

::: {.content-visible when-profile="scratch"}

### Sample

```{r}
#| label: lgi-age-sex-data
data_lgi_age_sex <-
  inner_join(global_lgi, demo, by = join_by(bblid), relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  select(lgi, age, sex) |>
  drop_na() |>
  mutate(
    sex_ord = ordered(sex, levels = c("Female", "Male")),
    age_c = age - mean(age)
  )
```

:::

### Predictor Association

```{r}
#| label: lgi-age-sex-test
t.test(
  age ~ sex,
  data = data_lgi_age_sex,
  var.equal = TRUE
)

plot_age_sex <-
  ggplot(
    data = data_lgi_age_sex,
    mapping = aes(x = age, group = sex, color = sex, fill = sex)
  ) +
  geom_histogram(position = "identity", binwidth = 1, alpha = 0.5) +
  theme_linedraw() +
  color_scale_sex +
  fill_scale_sex +
  labs(title = "Age Distribution by Sex", x = "Age", y = "Count")

plot_age_sex
```

::: {.content-visible when-profile="scratch"}

### Model Selection

#### Model 1: Additive Sex Effect with Linear and Nonlinear Age Components

This model tests whether age and sex are significantly associated with global LGI while allowing a nonlinear age effect. Both the linear and nonlinear components of age were significant, suggesting a nonlinear relationship between age and LGI after accounting for sex. Sex was also significant, with males exhibiting higher global LGI than females after accounting for age.

```{r}
#| label: lgi-age-sex-1
model_lgi_age_sex_1 <- gam(
  lgi ~ age_c + sex + s(age_c, m = c(2, 0)),
  data = data_lgi_age_sex,
  method = "ML"
)

summary(model_lgi_age_sex_1)
```

#### Model 2: Linear Interaction with Nonlinear Age Effect

This model tests whether a linear interaction between age and sex is significantly associated with global LGI while allowing a nonlinear age effect. The linear interaction was not significant, suggesting insufficient evidence that the relationship between age and LGI differs by sex. Both the linear and nonlinear components of age were significant, suggesting a nonlinear relationship between age and LGI. Sex was also significant, with males exhibiting higher global LGI than females after accounting for age.

```{r}
#| label: lgi-age-sex-2
model_lgi_age_sex_2 <- gam(
  lgi ~ age_c * sex + s(age_c, m = c(2, 0)),
  data = data_lgi_age_sex,
  method = "ML"
)

summary(model_lgi_age_sex_2)
```

#### Model 3: Linear and Nonlinear Interactions with Nonlinear Age Effect

This model tests whether linear and nonlinear interactions between age and sex are significantly associated with global LGI while allowing a nonlinear age effect. Neither the linear nor nonlinear interaction was significant, suggesting insufficient evidence that the relationship between age and LGI differs by sex. Both the linear and nonlinear components of age were significant, suggesting a nonlinear relationship between age and LGI. Sex was also significant, with males exhibiting higher global LGI than females after accounting for age.

```{r}
#| label: lgi-age-sex-3
model_lgi_age_sex_3 <- gam(
  lgi ~ age_c * sex +
    s(age_c, m = c(2, 0)) +
    s(age_c, m = c(2, 0), by = sex_ord),
  data = data_lgi_age_sex,
  method = "ML"
)

summary(model_lgi_age_sex_3)
```

#### AIC

All three models exhibited similar AIC values (ΔAIC < 2), indicating comparable model support. Model 1 had the lowest AIC, while Models 2 and 3 had nearly identical AIC values. Neither the linear nor nonlinear age × sex interaction was statistically significant, and the nonlinear interaction in Model 3 was effectively penalized to zero. Model 1 was therefore selected on the basis of both AIC and parsimony, retaining a nonlinear effect of age and a main effect of sex without an interaction.

```{r}
#| label: lgi-age-sex-selection
aic_lgi_age_sex <- report_aic(list(
  model_lgi_age_sex_1 = model_lgi_age_sex_1,
  model_lgi_age_sex_2 = model_lgi_age_sex_2,
  model_lgi_age_sex_3 = model_lgi_age_sex_3
))

aic_lgi_age_sex |>
  kbl(
    col.names = c("", "Formula", "df", "AIC", "ΔAIC"),
    digits = 2
  )
```

#### Check Final Model

```{r}
#| label: lgi-age-sex-final
model_lgi_age_sex_final <- gam(
  lgi ~ s(age) + sex,
  data = data_lgi_age_sex,
  method = "REML"
)

gam.check(model_lgi_age_sex_final)
```

:::

### Results

```{r}

prediction_lgi_age_sex <- data_lgi_age_sex |>
  summarise(

        min(age, na.rm = TRUE),

      )

    data = prediction_lgi_age_sex,
    mapping = aes(y = fit, ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
    alpha = 0.5,
    color = NA
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = prediction_lgi_age_sex,
    mapping = aes(y = fit),
    linewidth = 0.75
  ) +
  color_scale_sex +
  fill_scale_sex +
  labs(
    title = "LGI Developmental Trajectories by Sex",
    subtitle = model_lgi_age_sex_final |>

  ) +
```

## Global LGI ~ Age x Trauma {#two-age-trauma}

Age and trauma exposure were significantly positively correlated. When modeled together, both age and trauma exposure showed significant linear associations with global LGI. There was also a significant linear age × trauma interaction, indicating that the association between trauma exposure and global LGI varied with age. Although an additive model suggested a nonlinear association with age, this nonlinear effect was no longer significant after accounting for the interaction. A more flexible tensor product interaction was also not significant. The most parsimonious model supported by the data was therefore `lgi ~ age * trauma`.

::: {.content-visible when-profile="scratch"}

### Sample

```{r}
#| label: lgi-age-trauma-data
data_lgi_age_trauma <-
  global_lgi |>
  inner_join(demo, by = join_by(bblid), relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  inner_join(env, by = join_by(bblid), relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  select(lgi, age, trauma) |>
  drop_na() |>
  mutate(age_c = age - mean(age), trauma_c = trauma - mean(trauma))
```

:::

### Predictor Association

```{r}
#| label: lgi-age-trauma-test
test_age_trauma <-
  cor.test(data_lgi_age_trauma$age, data_lgi_age_trauma$trauma)

test_age_trauma

plot_age_trauma <-
  ggplot(data = data_lgi_age_trauma, aes(x = age, y = trauma)) +
  geom_point(
    position = position_jitter(height = 0.25),
    alpha = 0.25,
    size = 1
  ) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm",
    formula = y ~ x,
    se = TRUE,
    color = "black",
    fill = "black",
    linewidth = 0.75,
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Correlation of Age and Trauma",
    subtitle = report_correlation(test_age_trauma),
    x = "Age",
    y = "Trauma*",
    caption = str_c(
      "*Trauma exposure is a discrete variable (0–9).",
      "Jitter is applied solely for visualization.",
      sep = " "
    )
  ) +
  theme_linedraw() +
  theme(plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0))

plot_age_trauma
```

::: {.content-visible when-profile="scratch"}

### Model Selection

#### Model 1: Additive Linear and Nonlinear Effects

This model tests whether age and trauma exposure have significant linear and nonlinear associations with global LGI. Both the linear and nonlinear components of age are significant, suggesting a nonlinear relationship between age and LGI. Only the linear component of trauma exposure is significant, suggesting a linear relationship between trauma exposure and LGI.

```{r}
#| label: lgi-age-trauma-1
model_lgi_age_trauma_1 <- gam(
  lgi ~ age_c +
    trauma_c +
    s(age_c, m = c(2, 0)) +
    s(trauma_c, k = 7, m = c(2, 0)),
  data = data_lgi_age_trauma,
  method = "ML"
)

summary(model_lgi_age_trauma_1)
```

#### Model 2: Linear Interaction with Nonlinear Main Effects

This model tests whether a linear interaction between age and trauma exposure is significantly associated with global LGI while allowing nonlinear main effects of both predictors. The linear interaction was significant, suggesting that the association between trauma exposure and LGI varies with age. The linear components of both age and trauma exposure were significant, whereas neither nonlinear component was significant, suggesting insufficient evidence of additional nonlinearity.

```{r}
#| label: lgi-age-trauma-2
model_lgi_age_trauma_2 <- gam(
  lgi ~ age_c * trauma_c +
    s(age_c, m = c(2, 0)) +
    s(trauma_c, k = 7, m = c(2, 0)),
  data = data_lgi_age_trauma,
  method = "ML"
)

summary(model_lgi_age_trauma_2)
```

#### Model 3: Tensor Product Interaction with Nonlinear Main Effects

This model tests whether a potentially nonlinear interaction between age and trauma exposure is significantly associated with global LGI while allowing nonlinear main effects of both predictors. The tensor product interaction was not statistically significant, suggesting insufficient evidence of a more flexible interaction. The smooth effects of both age and trauma exposure were significant, with each having an edf of 1.000, suggesting approximately linear main effects.

```{r}
#| label: lgi-age-trauma-3
model_lgi_age_trauma_3 <- gam(
  lgi ~ s(age) +
    s(trauma, k = 7) +
    ti(age, trauma, k = c(10, 7)),
  data = data_lgi_age_trauma,
  method = "ML"
)

summary(model_lgi_age_trauma_3)
```

#### Model 4: Linear Main Effects with Linear Interaction
This model tests whether a linear interaction between age and trauma exposure is significantly associated with global LGI without allowing nonlinear effects. The linear interaction was significant, suggesting that the association between trauma exposure and LGI varies with age. Both age and trauma exposure were also significant predictors, with their effects depending on the value of the other predictor.

```{r}
#| label: lgi-age-trauma-4
model_lgi_age_trauma_4 <- gam(
  lgi ~ age * trauma,
  data = data_lgi_age_trauma,
  method = "ML"
)

summary(model_lgi_age_trauma_4)
```

#### AIC
All four models exhibited similar AIC values (ΔAIC < 2), indicating comparable model support. Models 2 and 4 had nearly identical AIC values and were preferred over the additive and tensor product interaction models. Both models supported a significant linear age × trauma interaction, while the nonlinear components in Model 2 were effectively penalized to zero. Model 4 was selected on the basis of parsimony, retaining linear effects of age and trauma exposure and their interaction without unnecessary nonlinear components.

```{r}
#| label: lgi-age-trauma-selection
aic_lgi_age_trauma <- report_aic(list(
  model_lgi_age_trauma_1 = model_lgi_age_trauma_1,
  model_lgi_age_trauma_2 = model_lgi_age_trauma_2,
  model_lgi_age_trauma_3 = model_lgi_age_trauma_3,
  model_lgi_age_trauma_4 = model_lgi_age_trauma_4
))

aic_lgi_age_trauma |>
  kbl(
    col.names = c("", "Formula", "df", "AIC", "ΔAIC"),
    digits = 2
  )
```

#### Check Final Model

```{r}
#| label: lgi-age-trauma-final
model_lgi_age_trauma_final <- gam(
  lgi ~ age * trauma,
  data = data_lgi_age_trauma,
  method = "REML"
)

gam.check(model_lgi_age_trauma_final)
```

## Global LGI ~ SES x Sex {#two-ses-sex}

SES differed significantly by sex, with males having higher SES than females on average. When modeled together, both SES and sex showed significant associations with global LGI, with higher SES associated with higher global LGI and males exhibiting higher global LGI than females after accounting for SES. There was insufficient evidence of a significant linear or nonlinear SES × sex interaction. Although a model allowing sex-specific nonlinear SES associations had the lowest AIC, its improvement over the simpler additive models was negligible. The most parsimonious model supported by the data was therefore `lgi ~ ses + sex`.

::: {.content-visible when-profile="scratch"}

### Sample

```{r}
#| label: lgi-ses-sex-data
data_lgi_ses_sex <-
  global_lgi |>
  inner_join(demo, by = join_by(bblid), relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  inner_join(env, by = join_by(bblid), relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  select(lgi, sex, ses) |>
  drop_na() |>
  mutate(
    sex_ord = ordered(sex, levels = c("Female", "Male")),
    ses_c = ses - mean(ses)
  )
```

:::

### Predictor Association

```{r}
#| label: lgi-ses-sex-test
t.test(
  ses ~ sex,
  data = data_lgi_ses_sex,
  var.equal = TRUE
)

plot_ses_sex <-
  ggplot(
    data = data_lgi_ses_sex,
    mapping = aes(x = ses, group = sex, color = sex, fill = sex)
  ) +
  geom_histogram(position = "identity", binwidth = 0.2, alpha = 0.5) +
  theme_linedraw() +
  color_scale_sex +
  fill_scale_sex +
  labs(title = "SES Distribution by Sex", x = "SES", y = "Count")

plot_ses_sex
```

::: {.content-visible when-profile="scratch"}

### Model Selection

#### Model 1: Additive Linear SES Effect and Sex Effect

This model tests whether SES and sex are significantly associated with global LGI without an interaction. Both SES and sex were significant predictors, with higher SES associated with higher global LGI and males exhibiting higher global LGI than females after accounting for SES.

```{r}
#| label: lgi-ses-sex-1
model_lgi_ses_sex_1 <- gam(
  lgi ~ ses + sex,
  data = data_lgi_ses_sex,
  method = "ML"
)

summary(model_lgi_ses_sex_1)
```

#### Model 2: Linear SES × Sex Interaction

This model tests whether a linear interaction between SES and sex is significantly associated with global LGI. The interaction was not significant, suggesting insufficient evidence that the relationship between SES and LGI differs by sex. Both SES and sex were significant predictors, with higher SES associated with higher global LGI and males exhibiting higher global LGI than females after accounting for SES.

```{r}
#| label: lgi-ses-sex-2
model_lgi_ses_sex_2 <- gam(
  lgi ~ ses * sex,
  data = data_lgi_ses_sex,
  method = "ML"
)

summary(model_lgi_ses_sex_2)
```

#### Model 3: Additive Linear and Nonlinear SES Effects with Sex Effect

This model tests whether SES and sex are significantly associated with global LGI while allowing a nonlinear SES effect. The nonlinear component of SES was not significant and was effectively penalized to zero, suggesting insufficient evidence of a nonlinear relationship between SES and LGI. Both the linear component of SES and sex were significant, with higher SES associated with higher global LGI and males exhibiting higher global LGI than females after accounting for SES.

```{r}
#| label: lgi-ses-sex-3
model_lgi_ses_sex_3 <- gam(
  lgi ~ ses_c + sex + s(ses_c, m = c(2, 0)),
  data = data_lgi_ses_sex,
  method = "ML"
)

summary(model_lgi_ses_sex_3)
```

#### Model 4: Linear and Nonlinear Interactions with Nonlinear SES Effect

This model tests whether linear and nonlinear interactions between SES and sex are significantly associated with global LGI while allowing a nonlinear SES effect. Neither the linear nor nonlinear interaction was significant, suggesting insufficient evidence that the relationship between SES and LGI differs by sex. The nonlinear component of SES was also not significant, suggesting a linear relationship between SES and LGI. Both the linear component of SES and sex were significant, with higher SES associated with higher global LGI and males exhibiting higher global LGI than females after accounting for SES.

```{r}
#| label: lgi-ses-sex-4
model_lgi_ses_sex_4 <- gam(
  lgi ~ ses_c * sex +
    s(ses_c, m = c(2, 0)) +
    s(ses_c, m = c(2, 0), by = sex_ord),
  data = data_lgi_ses_sex,
  method = "ML"
)

summary(model_lgi_ses_sex_4)
```

#### Model 5: Sex-Specific Nonlinear SES Effects

This model tests whether SES has potentially nonlinear associations with global LGI that differ by sex. Separate smooth functions are estimated for females and males. SES was significantly associated with global LGI in both sexes. The SES association exhibited some evidence of curvature in females (edf = 1.514), whereas the association in males was approximately linear (edf = 1.000). Sex was also significant, with males exhibiting higher global LGI after accounting for SES.

```{r}
#| label: lgi-ses-sex-5
model_lgi_ses_sex_5 <- gam(
  lgi ~ sex + s(ses, by = sex),
  data = data_lgi_ses_sex,
  method = "ML"
)

summary(model_lgi_ses_sex_5)
```

#### Model 6: Additive Nonlinear SES Effect and Sex Effect

This model tests whether SES and sex are significantly associated with global LGI while allowing a nonlinear SES effect without an interaction. The smooth effect of SES was significant but had an edf of 1.000, suggesting a linear relationship between SES and LGI. Sex was also significant, with males exhibiting higher global LGI than females after accounting for SES.

```{r}
#| label: lgi-ses-sex-6
model_lgi_ses_sex_6 <- gam(
  lgi ~ s(ses) + sex,
  data = data_lgi_ses_sex,
  method = "ML"
)

summary(model_lgi_ses_sex_6)
```

#### AIC

All six models exhibited similar AIC values (ΔAIC < 2), indicating comparable model support. Model 5 had the lowest AIC, although its improvement over Models 1, 3, and 6 was negligible (ΔAIC < 0.3). Models 3 and 6 supported a linear SES association, with their nonlinear components effectively penalized to zero. Neither the linear nor nonlinear SES × sex interaction was statistically significant in Model 4. Although Model 5 allowed sex-specific nonlinear SES associations, the additional complexity provided little improvement in model fit. Model 1 was therefore selected on the basis of parsimony and comparable AIC, retaining a linear effect of SES and a main effect of sex without an interaction.

```{r}
#| label: lgi-ses-sex-selection
aic_lgi_ses_sex <- report_aic(list(
  model_lgi_ses_sex_1 = model_lgi_ses_sex_1,
  model_lgi_ses_sex_2 = model_lgi_ses_sex_2,
  model_lgi_ses_sex_3 = model_lgi_ses_sex_3,
  model_lgi_ses_sex_4 = model_lgi_ses_sex_4,
  model_lgi_ses_sex_5 = model_lgi_ses_sex_5,
  model_lgi_ses_sex_6 = model_lgi_ses_sex_6
))

aic_lgi_ses_sex |>
  kbl(
    col.names = c("", "Formula", "df", "AIC", "ΔAIC"),
    digits = 2
  )
```

#### Check Final Model

```{r}
#| label: lgi-ses-sex-final
model_lgi_ses_sex_final <- gam(
  lgi ~ ses + sex,
  data = data_lgi_ses_sex,
  method = "REML"
)

gam.check(model_lgi_ses_sex_final)
```

:::

### Results

```{r}
#| label: lgi-ses-sex-results

      )
```
